# onpager_schedule_rotation (Resource)

Manage one primary rotation declaration for a schedule, independently of parent settings and sibling declarations.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Local timestamps use the provider request timezone. For example,
# timezone = "Europe/Moscow" resolves 09:00 to 06:00Z in the backend.
resource "onpager_schedule_rotation" "example" {
  schedule_id    = var.schedule_id
  effective_from = "2027-01-04T10:00:00"
  starts_at      = "2027-01-04T09:00:00"
  user_ids       = var.user_ids
  recurrence = {
    every = 1
    unit  = "weeks"
  }
}

variable "schedule_id" {
  description = "Existing enabled schedule UUID owned by an active team."
  type        = string
}

variable "user_ids" {
  description = "Ordered queue of distinct active team member UUIDs."
  type        = list(string)
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `effective_from` (String) Explicit publication boundary for this complete declaration: a whole-second local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` or explicit-offset RFC3339 timestamp; zero-only fractional digits are accepted. Source and UTC years must be 0001 through 9999. Independent of the `starts_at` recurrence anchor and never derived from the current time. Updates preserve the earlier plan, including gaps. Equivalent timestamp spellings retain the configured value across request-timezone response changes. Local input is sent unchanged and resolved by the backend in the provider request timezone; DST ambiguity or gaps return API diagnostics. Explicit offsets always identify absolute instants. Changing an explicit provider timezone plans an update for local input.
- `recurrence` (Attributes) Complete recurrence interval anchored at `starts_at`. Required; omission and `null` are invalid. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--recurrence))
- `schedule_id` (String) Owning schedule UUID. Changing it replaces this child declaration; parent settings and sibling rotations remain independent. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `starts_at` (String) Recurrence anchor for a primary rotation, or inclusive start for an override. Use a whole-second local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` or explicit-offset RFC3339 timestamp; zero-only fractional digits are accepted. Source and UTC years must be 0001 through 9999. Equivalent timestamp spellings retain the configured value across request-timezone response changes. Local input is sent unchanged and resolved by the backend in the provider request timezone; DST ambiguity or gaps return API diagnostics. Explicit offsets always identify absolute instants. Changing an explicit provider timezone plans an update for local input. Must precede `ends_at` when set.
- `user_ids` (List of String) Nonempty ordered list of distinct nonzero canonical lowercase user UUIDs. List order defines rotation order and is preserved. Users must be active members of the owning team; no membership is created implicitly.

### Optional

- `ends_at` (String) Exclusive whole-second end in local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` or explicit-offset RFC3339 form; zero-only fractional digits are accepted. Source and UTC years must be 0001 through 9999. Must follow `starts_at`. Primary rotations may omit this or use `null` for no end; overrides require a finite end. An empty string is invalid. Equivalent timestamp spellings retain the configured value across request-timezone response changes. Local input is sent unchanged and resolved by the backend in the provider request timezone; DST ambiguity or gaps return API diagnostics. Explicit offsets always identify absolute instants. Changing an explicit provider timezone plans an update for local input.
- `max_shift_duration_seconds` (Number) Optional positive whole-second shift-duration limit. Omission or `null` leaves shifts unrestricted by this limit; zero and negative values are invalid.
- `weekdays` (Set of String) Optional nonempty set of UTC weekdays: `MO`, `TU`, `WE`, `TH`, `FR`, `SA`, `SU`. Omission or `null` means unrestricted weekdays; an explicit empty set is invalid.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `request_timezone` (String) Explicit provider request timezone last applied to local datetime inputs. Null when the provider timezone is omitted or all inputs have explicit offsets. Changing the explicit provider timezone plans an update for local inputs; refresh alone preserves saved instants. The backend interprets local clocks and reports DST ambiguity or nonexistent times.
- `revision` (Number) This child rotation's revision, used in strong numeric `If-Match` for declaration replacement and retirement. Independent of parent settings, siblings, and aggregate revision. Stale writes report a conflict.

<a id="nestedatt--recurrence"></a>
### Nested Schema for `recurrence`

Required:

- `every` (Number) Recurrence multiplier from 1 through 2147483647; zero is invalid.
- `unit` (String) Recurrence unit: `hours`, `days`, `weeks`, or `months`.

## Import

Import using `schedule_uuid/rotation_uuid`. Import reads the latest surviving
declaration, independently of the current occurrence. A stopped rotation is
imported with its bounded `ends_at`.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_schedule_rotation.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_schedule_rotation.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222
```

## Lifecycle

This resource owns one primary rotation's participant queue and recurrence.
Participants must be active members of the owning team. Reference membership
resources in `user_ids` so Terraform creates memberships before the rotation and
retires the rotation before revoking them. List order defines rotation order.
Weekdays and recurrence use UTC.

`starts_at` anchors recurrence. The separate, required `effective_from` boundary
starts planned coverage on create and replaces coverage from that instant on
update, preserving earlier coverage and stopped gaps. Use a fixed timestamp or
input variable. Advancing this boundary changes the schedule; a moving
`timestamp()` expression republishes on each apply. Null `ends_at` leaves
coverage open-ended. Null `weekdays` or `max_shift_duration_seconds` removes
that constraint.

Refresh and import read the declaration with the greatest surviving effective
boundary, then publication number, independently of request time. Updates
publish the complete declaration using this rotation's own revision. Parent
settings and sibling revisions are independent. A stale revision requires a new
plan; the provider does not retry with a newer revision.

A committed write followed by a failed read retains its known identity and
revision. Before binding local timestamp inputs, the follow-up read must return
the exact committed child revision. A concurrent edit reports a conflict and
retains the committed receipt.

Destroy retires the rotation's complete planned coverage using `mode=all`,
retaining immutable rule versions and historical notification facts. Cleanup is
supported under inactive teams or schedules. Errors retain state. Confirmed
absence of surviving coverage removes the resource from state. Other rotations
and parent settings are managed separately.

## Timestamps and timezone

Timestamps use whole seconds; zero-only fractional digits are accepted. Use
local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` strings or RFC3339 with `Z` or an explicit offset.
Input is sent unchanged. The API resolves local values in the provider request
`timezone`, stores UTC, returns offset timestamps and rejects ambiguous or
nonexistent local times. Timezone conversion does not change UTC recurrence or
weekday rules.

State retains configured strings while private bindings to authoritative server
instants remain equivalent, including responses in a different request zone.
Changed instants appear as drift. Import adopts explicit-offset API values.
Configured strings and private bindings persist in Terraform state.

Changing an explicit provider `timezone` plans an update through computed
`request_timezone` when any configured boundary is local. Apply sends the same
strings in the new zone; refresh preserves stored instants. Explicit-offset-only
declarations do not require a write for a request-zone change. Omitted provider
timezone follows the API actor's default without explicit zone tracking.

## Permissions

Requires owning-team grants `schedule_rotations.create`,
`schedule_rotations.read`, `schedule_rotations.update`,
`schedule_rotations.publish_version` and `schedule_rotations.delete`. Update
requires both update and publish-version authority, plus read authority for the
follow-up read. Parent schedules and memberships require their separate grants.
